title: tera
text: Everything tera revolves around Tera object, serves template library encapsulated rendering methods. example, initialize Tera engine empty template library calling Tera$new() arguments. complicated directory system nested templates inheritance patterns - common situation web development, may find easier initialize tera specifying directory glob pattern. Suppose, example, website directory looks like : can generate new Tera around directory like
code: template_dir <- system.file("templates", package = "tera")  cat(   "website",   list.files(template_dir, recursive = TRUE),   sep = "\n- " ) website - base.html - blog/post.html - components.html - hello.html - index.html tera <- Tera$new(file.path(template_dir, "**/*.html")) tera ## ── Tera ── ## Template library: ## • base.html ## • blog/post.html ## • components.html ## • hello.html ## • index.html ##  ## Globals: 0 ## Components: 2 ## Autoescape: TRUE ## Delimiters: {% Block %}, {{ Variable }}, {# Comment #}

text: Templates can added file string. initialize tera instance glob add file templates template directory, can reload glob catch new templates. Reset continue built-template examples.
code: # add templates manually from file tera <- Tera$new() tera$add_file_templates( "base.html" = file.path(template_dir, "base.html"), "index.html" = file.path(template_dir, "index.html") ) tera ## ── Tera ── ## Template library: ## • base.html ## • index.html ## ## Globals: 0 ## Components: 0 ## Autoescape: TRUE ## Delimiters: {% Block %}, {{ Variable }}, {# Comment #} # add templates manually from string tera$add_string_templates( img = '' ) tera ## ── Tera ── ## Template library: ## • base.html ## • img ## • index.html ## ## Globals: 0 ## Components: 0 ## Autoescape: TRUE ## Delimiters: {% Block %}, {{ Variable }}, {# Comment #} example_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "tera-templates") dir.create(example_dir) file.copy( from = file.path(template_dir, "base.html"), to = file.path(example_dir, "base.html") ) ## [1] TRUE tera <- Tera$new(file.path(example_dir, "*.html")) tera ## ── Tera ── ## Template library: ## • base.html ## ## Globals: 0 ## Components: 0 ## Autoescape: TRUE ## Delimiters: {% Block %}, {{ Variable }}, {# Comment #} file.copy( from = file.path(template_dir, "index.html"), to = file.path(example_dir, "index.html") ) ## [1] TRUE tera$reload() tera ## ── Tera ── ## Template library: ## • base.html ## • index.html ## ## Globals: 0 ## Components: 0 ## Autoescape: TRUE ## Delimiters: {% Block %}, {{ Variable }}, {# Comment #} tera <- Tera$new(file.path(template_dir, "**/*.html"))

title: tera
text: Generally speaking, rendering template involves supplying context, set key-value pairs, keys variable names - surrounded {{ variable }} template - values content inject template. can render template string file. Consider hypothetical website’s index template: four variables: {{ title }}, {{ x }}, {{ y }}, {{ owner }}. can render template string passing context, set values variables. render template string. can also render template file specifying outfile. can render specific block template: can also render individual components defined one templates, example can bypass library templates altogether pass template string directly Two helper functions also provided want render one-template without going throught process initializing tera instance. render_template() function render template file, render_string() render string, methods, without explicit tera instance.
code:
template_dir |> file.path("index.html") |> readLines(warn = FALSE) |> cat(sep = "\n") {% extends "base.html" %} {% block content %}

{{ title }}

{{ p }}.

{% endblock content %} {% block footer %}

Copyright 2026 by {{ owner }}.

{% endblock footer %} string <- tera$render_template( "index.html", title = "This is my blog", p = "Welcome to my awesome homepage.", owner = "Blake" ) cat(string)

This is my blog

Welcome to my awesome homepage..

title: tera
text: Tera templating engine offers lot additional functionality, like control flow data manipulation. example, blog post template shows construct loop apply built-filters functions. {{ now() | date(format="%Y-%m-%d") }}, now() function returns current date time. ’s returned value piped date() filter, provides formatting options. R, one way achieving thing format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d"). template also -loop construction {$ product products %} allows looping elements product table array. passed data.frame, get :
code:
template_dir |> file.path("blog", "post.html") |> readLines(warn = FALSE) |> cat(sep = "\n") {% extends "base.html" %} {% block content -%}

{{ title }}

Last updated: {{ now() | date(format="%Y-%m-%d") }}.

    {%- for product in products %}
  • {{ product.name }}: {{ product.price }}
    • {%- endfor %}
{%- endblock content %} products <- data.frame( name = c("apple", "banana", "orange"), price = c(0.25, 0.4, 0.5) ) string <- tera$render_template( "blog/post.html", title = "Fruit prices", products = products ) cat(string)

Fruit prices

Last updated: 2026-09-14.

  • apple: 0.25
  • banana: 0.4
  • orange: 0.5

title: tera
text: Tera escapes HTML default: one-rendering like , function takes autoescape argument. rendering templates components library, can turn autoescape globally using $autoescape_off() turn back $autoescape_on() (default).
code: string <- tera$render_string(   "{{ html }}",   html = "<script>alert('Hello World!')</script>" )  cat(string) <script>alert('Hello World!')</script> string <- tera$render_string(   "{{ html }}",   html = "<script>alert('Hello World!')</script>",   autoescape = FALSE )  cat(string) <script>alert('Hello World!')</script> tera$autoescape_off() tera$autoescape_on()

text: Templates marked {% %} blocks, { } variables, {# #} comments. can change $set_delimiters(), though engine empty template library, must done templates added. start delimiter must differ others, delimiter must exactly two bytes long, delimiter left NULL unchanged. Use $delimiters() see current set.
code: alt <- Tera$new()  alt$set_delimiters(   variable_start = "<<",   variable_end = ">>" )  alt$render_string("<< greeting >>, world!", greeting = "Hello") [1] "Hello, world!" alt$delimiters() $block_start [1] "{%"  $block_end [1] "%}"  $variable_start [1] "<<"  $variable_end [1] ">>"  $comment_start [1] "{#"  $comment_end [1] "#}"

title: Tera Templating Engine
text: tera package uses extendr provide access Vincent Prouillet’s Tera templating engine Rust. Users mainly interact Tera R6 object, serves template library encapsulated methods rendering templates given context. Template syntax supports additional logic, including built-filters, tests, functions, well loops, conditions, inheritance. Documentation Tera’s templating syntax can found https://keats.github.io/tera/.

text: Tera templating engine rendering templates contexts consisting variables values. Similar glue, additional template logic. glob pattern templates/*.html match files .html extension located directly inside templates folder, templates/**/*.html match files .html extension directly inside subdirectory templates. default naming convention give template full relative path templates (whatever template directory called). initialized glob, template names take path file template relative base template directory. example, pass templates/**/*.html, template file templates/blog/post.html name blog/post.html. specified manually, templates must named. true context variables. possible add variables global context can accessed template. See set_globals() method.
